_comment: Shoulder corridor: rotator-cuff strain, post-op shoulder, early frozen-shoulder rehab. Instructions and art authored in-house for the Carryover seed library.

exercises.name: Pendulum Swings
instructions: Lean forward and rest your good hand on a chair back or counter, letting the affected arm hang straight down, completely relaxed.
Shift your body weight in small circles so the hanging arm swings gently like a pendulum — the arm itself does no work.
Let the swing trace small circles both directions, then easy front-to-back and side-to-side lines.
Keep the motion small and pain-free; this is relaxed movement, not effort.

exercises.name: External Rotation Isometric
instructions: Stand in a doorway with your elbow bent to a right angle and tucked against your side, forearm pointing forward.
Place the back of your wrist against the doorframe.
Press the wrist outward into the frame as if rotating the arm away from your belly — nothing should actually move.
Build to a firm but comfortable pressure, hold steady while breathing normally, then release slowly. Sharp pain means back off the effort.

exercises.name: Internal Rotation Isometric
instructions: Stand at the edge of a doorway with the affected side closest to the frame, elbow bent to a right angle and tucked against your ribs.
Place your palm against the doorframe, forearm pointing forward.
Press the palm into the frame as if turning your hand toward your belly — the arm should not actually move.
Build to a firm, comfortable pressure, hold while breathing normally, then ease off slowly. Keep the shoulder itself quiet and relaxed.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeeze
instructions: Sit tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Draw your shoulder blades back and down, as if tucking them into your back pockets.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears — this is a squeeze between the blades, not a shrug.
Hold the squeeze while breathing normally, then let everything go fully slack before the next one.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height and stand side-on so the band crosses in front of your belly, working elbow bent to a right angle and tucked to your side.
Optionally squeeze a small rolled towel between the elbow and your ribs to keep the elbow glued in place.
Keeping the elbow pinned, rotate the forearm outward away from your belly, like a gate swinging open.
Pause briefly, then return with control — the way back should be just as slow as the way out.
If the elbow drifts from your side or the shoulder hikes, the band is too heavy.

exercises.name: Band Row
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at chest height around something sturdy and hold an end in each hand, arms reaching forward.
Stand tall and start the pull by drawing your shoulder blades together.
Pull the hands in toward your lower ribs, elbows brushing past your sides.
Keep the shoulders down away from the ears and the neck relaxed throughout.
Let the arms reach forward again slowly, allowing the blades to glide apart at the very end.

exercises.name: Wall Slide
instructions: Stand facing a wall and rest both hands on it at shoulder height — a folded towel under the hands helps them glide.
Slide the hands upward along the wall, letting your body lean gently in as the arms rise.
Go only as high as stays comfortable; the shoulders should stay relaxed, not hiked toward the ears.
Slide back down to shoulder height with the same control.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
instructions: Lie on your unaffected side with a light dumbbell in the top hand, top elbow bent to a right angle and resting on your ribs.
Place a small rolled towel between the elbow and your side to hold the arm in a friendly position.
Keeping the elbow pinned to the towel, rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling, like a gate swinging open.
Lower back down slowly — take more time on the way down than the way up.
Stop short of any pinching, and end the set if anything feels sharp — the range that stays smooth is the right range.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
instructions: Lie on your affected side with that shoulder stacked directly beneath you and the arm out in front, elbow bent to a right angle, fingers pointing to the ceiling.
With the opposite hand, gently guide the back of the affected wrist down toward the floor.
Push only to a gentle stretch across the back of the shoulder — never into pinching pain at the front.
Hold there, breathing slowly, then release the pressure before rolling off the shoulder.

exercises.name: Doorway Pec Stretch
instructions: Stand in a doorway and place your forearm along the frame, elbow at shoulder height and bent to a right angle.
Step the same-side foot forward until you feel a gentle stretch across the front of the chest and shoulder.
Keep the ribs down and avoid arching the lower back — the stretch belongs in the chest, not the spine.
Hold, breathing easy, then step back to release.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up Plus
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your hands flat on it at shoulder height, feet a step back so your body makes one straight line.
Bend the elbows to lower your chest toward the wall slowly — the lowering is where the control lives.
Push back to arm's length, then keep going: spread the shoulder blades apart and push your upper back away from the wall. That extra push is the plus.
Keep the neck long and the body in one line; if the shoulders start to shrug or the low back sags, step closer to the wall.

exercises.name: Prone T Raise
instructions: Lie face down with your arms out to the sides at shoulder level, thumbs pointing to the ceiling, forehead resting on the floor or a folded towel.
Set the shoulder blades back and down, then float both arms up off the floor.
Lift from between the shoulder blades, not by cranking the neck or arching the low back.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until the arms rest again.

progressions.note: Progress when the arm swings relaxed for a couple of minutes with pain at 2/10 or less.
Progress when the hands glide above shoulder height without shrugging and with no pain flare the next day.
Add once a full session of swinging is pain-free and reaching to shoulder height stays at 3/10 or below.
Progress when a firm press holds for the full count at 2/10 pain or less across several consecutive days.
Progress when every repetition ends with the elbow still pinned to the side and any soreness clears by the next morning.
Progress when the squeeze holds for the full count without the shoulders creeping up toward the ears.
Progress when the final repetitions of a set stay as smooth as the first, with the neck relaxed throughout.
